packages.name: Shopware 6.6
packages.description: Shopware asynchronous payment handler. Initial integration build; native-store staging and real-payment acceptance required.
packages.installation:
1. Upload this ZIP under Extensions > My extensions, or extract the `MochiPay` folder into `custom/plugins/MochiPay`.
2. From the Shopware root run `bin/console plugin:refresh` and `bin/console plugin:install --activate MochiPay`.
3. Open the extension configuration. Enter credentials and enable MochiPay. Settings can be scoped to a sales channel; set them for each channel using this gateway.
4. Enable the MochiPay payment method in Settings > Payment methods and assign it to the desired sales channels. Clear the cache.
5. Place a staging order and complete the saved checkout.

Install only this package on Shopware 6.6. Shopware 6.7 uses a different handler API and has a separate ZIP. The method is created inactive and retains its identifier/history across in-place updates. Switching to 6.7 requires replacing the plugin files with the 6.7 package and updating the plugin normally.

packages.name: Shopware 6.7
packages.description: Shopware AbstractPaymentHandler. Initial integration build; native-store staging and real-payment acceptance required.
packages.installation:
1. Upload this ZIP under Extensions > My extensions, or extract `MochiPay` into `custom/plugins/MochiPay`.
2. Run `bin/console plugin:refresh` and `bin/console plugin:install --activate MochiPay` from the store root.
3. Configure the extension: credentials, Enabled and unique amount direction. Set the configuration for every sales channel that uses this gateway.
4. Enable its payment method under Settings > Payment methods and assign it to the sales channels. Clear the cache.
5. Complete staging acceptance before enabling customer traffic.

Use this ZIP only with Shopware 6.7. Do not install both Shopware packages. For an existing 6.6 installation, back up configuration and attempt/history tables, upgrade Shopware, replace plugin files with this package and run the normal `plugin:update MochiPay` process. The payment-method identifier remains the same and update does not reset Enabled settings.

packages.name: Drupal Commerce
packages.php_envelope: Drupal 9.3–9.5: PHP 7.4–8.1; Drupal 10: PHP 8.1–8.3; Drupal 11: PHP 8.3–8.4, only when allowed by the exact Drupal release
packages.description: Commerce offsite payment gateway and completed commerce_payment entity. Initial integration build; native-store staging and real-payment acceptance required.

core_requirements.php: 7.4–8.1 within exact core requirements
8.1–8.3; later Drupal 10 releases may require 8.3
8.3–8.4 only where allowed by the exact core/dependency lock

packages.installation:
1. Extract `mochipay` into `web/modules/custom/mochipay` (or `modules/custom/mochipay` if your document root is the project root).
2. Enable the module: `drush en mochipay -y`, then `drush cr`. The installer creates the attempt table without resetting an existing table.
3. Under Commerce > Configuration > Payment gateways, add a gateway using the MochiPay plugin. Choose native gateway mode Live; this is the default. It is independent of ON_SITE/HPP.
4. Enable the gateway entity, enter credentials in its configuration, check Enabled, keep the desired currency/network choices and save. Attach any normal Commerce conditions you need.
5. The public endpoint is `/mochipay/checkout/{gateway-machine-name}`. It is capability-scoped and excludes caching. Do not put authentication or a WAF challenge in front of its callbacks.

The same module uses the supported Commerce annotation discovery fallback in both major lines. Choose PHP according to Drupal core and your Commerce dependencies. Drupal 9.3 with PHP 7.3 is outside this module's range. A later Drupal 10 release that requires PHP 8.3 must run 8.3. The custom attempt table is deliberately retained on uninstall; it is not a hook_schema-managed table.

packages.name: EC-CUBE 4.3
packages.description: PaymentMethodInterface with native PurchaseFlow prepare/commit. Initial integration build; native-store staging and real-payment acceptance required.
packages.installation:
1. Upload this ZIP using EC-CUBE's local plugin installation screen. Its `composer.json` is at the ZIP root, as required by the installer. Enable the MochiPay plugin.
2. Open its Settings link on the plugin list, or `/{your-admin-path}/mochipay/config`. Enter credentials, enable it and save.
3. Under Shop settings > Payment methods, associate the new MochiPay method with the relevant delivery methods. Normal EC-CUBE delivery/payment restrictions still apply.
4. Clear the EC-CUBE cache. Run staging checkout in ON_SITE and HPP.

This package targets EC-CUBE 4.3; it does not target 2.x/3.x/4.0–4.2. Core checkout currency is JPY. The amount is the native payment total including charges, not a recomputed subtotal. The native order stays Pending until a verified PAID result commits PurchaseFlow and records the payment date. The callback does not trust a supplied order number. A buyer's own completion endpoint restores the native order-completion session. PostgreSQL and MySQL/MariaDB are supported; SQLite is outside this build.

packages.name: Bagisto 2.3
packages.php_envelope: PHP 8.2.x / 8.3.x / 8.4.x (also satisfy the store dependency lock)
packages.description: Laravel package and Webkul payment adapter with native order/invoice repositories. Initial integration build; native-store staging and real-payment acceptance required.

core_requirements.php: PHP 8.2.x / 8.3.x / 8.4.x (also satisfy the store dependency lock)

packages.installation:
1. Extract the `MochiPay` folder to `packages/MochiPay` in the Bagisto project.
2. Register a local Composer path repository in the project's composer.json: `{"type":"path","url":"packages/MochiPay","options":{"symlink":false}}`. Keep existing repositories.
3. Run `composer require mochipay/bagisto-payment:1.0.0`, `php artisan migrate --force` and `php artisan optimize:clear`. Laravel package discovery registers the service provider; no vendor/core edits are needed. If package discovery is disabled, register `MochiPay\Bagisto\Providers\MochiPayServiceProvider` using the app's normal provider configuration.
4. Open Configure > Sales > Payment methods > MochiPay. Set API credentials, enable it, choose direction and save. Configuration is global to the package so asynchronous callbacks do not depend on a browser's channel selection.
5. The checkout is `/mochipay/checkout`; the initial native redirect is `/mochipay/redirect`. Exempt only this capability-scoped checkout endpoint from CSRF middleware, if your application has added a custom middleware class not already excluded by the package. The endpoint validates its own random attempt token and start nonce.

The adapter collects native cart totals and creates one pending order and attempt together in a transaction. Duplicate redirects reuse the attempt. The cart is deactivated after the order is saved. A verified payment records its remote identifier, updates the native order and creates the payable native invoice once. MySQL/MariaDB is required by this build.

packages.name: Sylius 2.0
packages.php_envelope: PHP 8.2.x / 8.3.x / 8.4.x (also satisfy the store dependency lock)
packages.description: Payum gateway factory/actions and Sylius payment state machine. Initial integration build; native-store staging and real-payment acceptance required.

core_requirements.php: PHP 8.2.x / 8.3.x / 8.4.x (also satisfy the store dependency lock)

packages.installation:
1. Extract `MochiPaySylius` to `plugins/MochiPaySylius` in your Sylius project. Add a Composer path repository for `plugins/MochiPaySylius`, preserving existing repositories, then run `composer require mochipay/sylius-plugin:1.0.0`.
2. Register `MochiPay\Sylius\MochiPayBundle::class => ['all' => true]` in `config/bundles.php`.
3. Add a routing resource to `config/routes/mochipay.yaml`: `mochipay: { resource: '@MochiPayBundle/Resources/config/routes.yaml' }`.
4. Run `bin/console cache:clear` and `bin/console mochipay:install`. The command creates/retains attempt storage; it does not change existing payments.
5. In the Sylius admin, create a payment method using gateway factory MochiPay. Set credentials in its gateway configuration, check Enable MochiPay, set direction, enable the native payment method and assign channels.
6. Complete native shop checkout acceptance. The public capability endpoint is `/mochipay/checkout`.

Use the Payum checkout integration provided by Sylius 2.0. A custom headless payment-request implementation needs to call the same native capture actions rather than bypassing them. Amounts are converted exactly from integer minor units using Symfony Intl's currency fraction digits. Capture/convert/status actions preserve native payment details; verified payment applies the native COMPLETE transition. MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL are supported. This package does not cover Sylius 1.x or 2.1+ interfaces.

packages.name: osCommerce 4.14
packages.php_envelope: PHP 7.4.x–8.3.x, subject to the installed osCommerce release and dependency lock
packages.description: ModulePayment, platform configuration and native OrdersPayment ledger. Initial integration build; native-store staging and real-payment acceptance required.

core_requirements.core: osCommerce 4.14.x; native V4 orderPayment module API
core_requirements.php: PHP 7.4.x–8.3.x, subject to the installed osCommerce release and dependency lock

packages.installation:
1. Back up the store, then copy the ZIP's `lib` folder into your osCommerce 4 application root. Keep the hierarchy: `lib/common/modules/orderPayment/mochipay.php` and `lib/common/modules/orderPayment/lib/MochiPay/`.
2. In the admin, open payment modules, install MochiPay for the required platform and edit its settings.
3. Enter the key and secret, set Enable MochiPay to True, choose direction, and save. Secret configuration uses osCommerce's native encrypted-key support. Defaults are ON_SITE and all five currencies.
4. Pick the native Paid order status if your store has a separate fulfillment state; value 0 uses the platform default. Paid/unpaid accounting is always stored separately in the native OrdersPayment ledger.
5. Verify the native callback route `callback/webhooks.payment.mochipay` is public. The saved URL contains the private attempt token, so do not replace it with a hand-written callback URL.
6. Run staging checkout and duplicate-notification checks. Each platform's saved payment uses that platform's credentials and is verified against its order ownership.

This is an osCommerce V4 module, targeting the 4.14 line. It is not an osCommerce 2.x/3.x adapter. The native pending debit is saved before payment starts; only a signed, matched PAID query updates that exact ledger entry to SUCCESSFUL. Amount conversion uses the order's saved currency rate and the native currency's decimal places. Whole orders only; partial invoices and store-credit mixed balances require separate handling.

packages.name: thirty bees 1.6
packages.php_envelope: PHP 7.4.x / 8.0.x / 8.1.x / 8.2.x / 8.3.x; use the matching thirty bees distribution
packages.description: PaymentModule, native waiting state and OrderHistory payment transition. Initial integration build; native-store staging and real-payment acceptance required.

core_requirements.php: PHP 7.4.x / 8.0.x / 8.1.x / 8.2.x / 8.3.x; use the matching thirty bees distribution

packages.installation:
1. Upload this ZIP in Modules > Add a new module, or extract `mochipay` into the store's `modules/mochipay` directory.
2. Install MochiPay. The installer creates a non-paid “Awaiting MochiPay payment” order state and retained attempt storage.
3. Open Configure, enter credentials, enable the gateway, choose direction and save. Currency/network choices and ON_SITE are already selected.
4. In the native payment restrictions, allow the desired countries, customer groups and fiat currencies. Keep the native Payment accepted status configured correctly.
5. Clear cache and run checkout. The initial form validates a native session token; the saved payment endpoint uses its private attempt capability.

The adapter targets thirty bees 1.6 and uses its actual `getOrderByCartId` API. It does not overwrite the core static `Module::isEnabled` method. Split-cart orders are refused for review. A verified PAID result updates the native order history once. Configuration, waiting state and attempt records are retained on uninstall.
